arc202_b.complexity: O(H log H + H log W) dominated by factorials/gcd scan

independent_oracle.type: direct enumeration of all +/- move words for small torus boards

proof_equivalent_invariant: If H is even, row coordinate under -2 never reaches all H rows, so no tour.
For odd H, reindex rows so every move advances one layer. A Hamiltonian successor map must be a bijection from every layer to the next.
For odd W, a bijection y->y+/-1 on the W-cycle must be all + or all -, so the H-layer return map is translation by s=2p-H and is one W-cycle iff gcd(s,W)=1.

For even W, a layer bijection has one of four period-2 sign patterns. It flips parity; after odd H layers the return map flips parity, and its square translates Z_(W/2) by S=#all_plus-#all_minus. It is one W-cycle iff gcd(S,W/2)=1.
The coefficient count for even W is [x^S](x+x^-1+2)^H = C(2H,H+S).

arc202_c.complexity: O(M log M log MOD + sum tau(A_i)) with M=max A_i<=200000

independent_oracle.type: Python arbitrary-precision repunit gcd/lcm prefix oracle

proof_equivalent_invariant: For any prime q, the cyclotomic indices d for which q divides Phi_d(10) lie on a divisibility chain (the standard q-power extension of ord_q(10), with the repunit denominator special case also chain-structured).
Therefore for a set of selected n, the q-adic valuation of the product of Phi_d(10) over the union of their divisor indices equals max v_q(R_n), hence exactly the LCM.
MOD=998244353 is prime and ord_MOD(10)=998244352>200000, so all required modular cyclotomic divisions are by nonzero residues.
